name: SmoothLife
miniText: Which features of Life-like organization survive when binary states become continuous values? NetLogo SmoothLife averages a patch field over an inner disk and surrounding annulus, then uses smooth sigmoid transitions to calculate the next generation. Rafler's original preprint [1] supplies the direct rule provenance, Wolfram [2] provides cellular-automaton context, and Fisch and colleagues [3] connect neighborhood thresholds with excitable pattern formation. The NetLogo Info explicitly retains discrete time and approximates continuous space with a finite grid. It also omits very small state contributions as a numerical optimization. Radius, transition widths, and birth and survival intervals affect whether moving structures persist. The simulation illustrates a parameterized generalization of local rule-driven organization; organic appearance does not identify living behavior, and a discretized update is not an exact simulation of every continuous formulation.
